name: Consolidated AUP
headers: Policy statement for NDIA ICT Acceptable Use Policy
rows: 01 Age Discrimination Act 2004
ADA-01
Prevent age discrimination in employment-related digital communications and ICT-enabled work practices.
Objects and unlawful discrimination provisions, including ss 3, 14-18.
The AUP must prohibit conduct over email, collaboration tools, messaging and systems that could support discriminatory treatment in the workplace.
Applies to NDIA as an APS employer and to all users communicating through NDIA ICT.
Respectful ICT use
Users must not use NDIA ICT to treat a person less favourably, exclude, ridicule or disadvantage a person because of their age.
https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A01302/latest
01 Age Discrimination Act 2004
ADA-02
Ensure NDIA digital services, forms, portals and communications do not create unreasonable age-based barriers.
Services, facilities and administration of Commonwealth laws or programs, including ss 28, 31 and 32.
The AUP should require inclusive digital behaviour because NDIA administers a Commonwealth program and uses ICT to provide services to the public.
Applies to NDIA staff and contractors who create, publish, send or maintain information for participants, providers, staff or the public.
Digital accessibility and inclusion
Users must design, publish and share NDIA digital information so that it does not unjustifiably exclude or disadvantage people because of age.
https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A01302/latest
01 Age Discrimination Act 2004
ADA-03
Avoid age-based assumptions, stereotypes or profiling in data, analytics, AI-assisted outputs or communications unless lawful and approved.
Direct and indirect discrimination concepts, ss 14-16.
The AUP should control user behaviour in systems and analytics to prevent discriminatory outcomes arising from ICT use.
Applies where NDIA users prepare analysis, case notes, decision-support material or communications using NDIA systems.
Data use and decision support
Users must not record, search, profile or make recommendations about a person based on age stereotypes or irrelevant age assumptions.
https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A01302/latest
02 APS Values Code Conduct
APS-VCE-01
Use Commonwealth resources properly and for a proper purpose.
Public Service Act 1999 s 13 and APSC Code of Conduct guidance.
The AUP is the primary policy control for proper use of NDIA ICT, devices, accounts, networks and information resources.

NDIA is a corporate Commonwealth entity responsible for managing the NDIS. NDIA staff are engaged under the Public Service Act, and the AUP should also bind contractors, partners and any person using NDIA ICT.
Proper use of ICT resources
Users must use NDIA ICT for authorised work purposes; any limited personal use must be lawful, reasonable, low risk and not interfere with work or NDIA systems.
https://www.apsc.gov.au/working-aps/integrity/integrity-resources/code-of-conduct
02 APS Values Code Conduct
APS-VCE-02
Comply with all applicable Australian laws and lawful and reasonable directions when using ICT.
Public Service Act 1999 s 13(4)-(5); APSC Code of Conduct elements.
The AUP must make legal compliance and following authorised ICT directions an explicit condition of access.

NDIA is a corporate Commonwealth entity responsible for managing the NDIS. NDIA staff are engaged under the Public Service Act, and the AUP should also bind contractors, partners and any person using NDIA ICT.
User responsibilities
Users must comply with all laws, NDIA policies and authorised ICT, security, privacy and records directions when using NDIA ICT.
https://www.apsc.gov.au/working-aps/integrity/integrity-resources/code-of-conduct
02 APS Values Code Conduct
APS-VCE-03
Behave honestly, with integrity, care and diligence, and in a way that upholds the APS Values and the reputation of the APS and NDIA.
APS Values and Code of Conduct guidance; Public Service Act ss 10 and 13.
Digital conduct can affect public trust; the AUP should set behavioural standards for email, chat, meetings, file sharing and online services.

NDIA is a corporate Commonwealth entity responsible for managing the NDIS. NDIA staff are engaged under the Public Service Act, and the AUP should also bind contractors, partners and any person using NDIA ICT.
Professional and ethical conduct
Users must communicate and act through NDIA ICT in a professional, honest, respectful and careful way that protects trust in the NDIA and the APS.
https://www.apsc.gov.au/working-aps/aps-values-code-conduct-and-employment-principles
02 APS Values Code Conduct
APS-VCE-04
Do not improperly use inside information, duties, status, power or authority.
Public Service Act 1999 s 13(10)-(11); APSC Code of Conduct elements.
The AUP must prohibit misuse of information obtained through NDIA systems for personal advantage or to harm others.

NDIA is a corporate Commonwealth entity responsible for managing the NDIS. NDIA staff are engaged under the Public Service Act, and the AUP should also bind contractors, partners and any person using NDIA ICT.
Misuse of information
Users must not use NDIA information, access, role or system privileges to gain a personal benefit, benefit another person or cause detriment to any person or the NDIA.
https://www.apsc.gov.au/working-aps/integrity/integrity-resources/code-of-conduct
02 APS Values Code Conduct
APS-VCE-05
Treat everyone with respect and courtesy and without harassment.
Public Service Act 1999 s 13(3); APS Employment Principles and Code guidance.
The AUP should translate APS behavioural obligations into rules for digital channels.

NDIA is a corporate Commonwealth entity responsible for managing the NDIS. NDIA staff are engaged under the Public Service Act, and the AUP should also bind contractors, partners and any person using NDIA ICT.
Respectful ICT use
Users must not use NDIA email, messaging, meetings, collaboration platforms or social media to bully, harass, intimidate, humiliate or abuse anyone.
https://www.apsc.gov.au/working-aps/integrity/integrity-resources/code-of-conduct
03 APS Employment Code Conduct
APS-EPC-01
Uphold APS Values in all official digital activity, including impartiality, commitment to service, accountability, respect, ethics and stewardship.
Public Service Act 1999 ss 10, 10A and 13; APSC APS Values guidance.
The AUP should express that digital conduct is official conduct when NDIA ICT is used.

NDIA is a corporate Commonwealth entity responsible for managing the NDIS. NDIA staff are engaged under the Public Service Act, and the AUP should also bind contractors, partners and any person using NDIA ICT.
APS values in digital conduct
Users must ensure their use of NDIA ICT is impartial, respectful, ethical, accountable and focused on NDIA business and participant outcomes.
https://www.apsc.gov.au/working-aps/aps-values-code-conduct-and-employment-principles
03 APS Employment Code Conduct
APS-EPC-02
Maintain confidentiality and protect official information obtained through APS employment.
Public Service Act 1999 s 13(6) and Code of Conduct guidance.
Confidentiality is central to acceptable use because NDIA systems hold sensitive participant, provider, staff and government information.

NDIA is a corporate Commonwealth entity responsible for managing the NDIS. NDIA staff are engaged under the Public Service Act, and the AUP should also bind contractors, partners and any person using NDIA ICT.
Confidentiality
Users must only access, use, discuss or disclose NDIA information where they are authorised and have a genuine work need.
https://www.apsc.gov.au/working-aps/integrity/integrity-resources/code-of-conduct
03 APS Employment Code Conduct
APS-EPC-03
Avoid real, potential or perceived conflicts of interest in ICT access and data use.
Public Service Act 1999 s 13(7) and APSC Code guidance.
AUP rules should prevent users from accessing records involving themselves, family, friends, external interests or conflicts unless authorised.

NDIA is a corporate Commonwealth entity responsible for managing the NDIS. NDIA staff are engaged under the Public Service Act, and the AUP should also bind contractors, partners and any person using NDIA ICT.
Conflicts and need-to-know access
Users must not access or use NDIA records where they have a personal interest unless they have disclosed the interest and obtained written authorisation.
https://www.apsc.gov.au/working-aps/integrity/integrity-resources/code-of-conduct
03 APS Employment Code Conduct
APS-EPC-04
Do not provide false or misleading information in response to an official request.
Public Service Act 1999 s 13(9).
Acceptable use must require accurate information in service desks, access requests, attestations, security incidents and records.

NDIA is a corporate Commonwealth entity responsible for managing the NDIS. NDIA staff are engaged under the Public Service Act, and the AUP should also bind contractors, partners and any person using NDIA ICT.
Accurate records and attestations
Users must provide complete, accurate and truthful information in NDIA systems, ICT requests, access reviews, records and incident reports.
https://www.apsc.gov.au/working-aps/integrity/integrity-resources/code-of-conduct
04 Archives Act 1983
ARC-01
Do not destroy, delete, alter, transfer or dispose of Commonwealth records unless authorised.
Archives Act 1983 record disposal controls, including s 24 and authorised disposal arrangements.
The AUP must prevent users from deleting or moving official digital records outside authorised processes.
NDIA creates and holds Commonwealth records in email, case systems, shared drives, collaboration tools and business applications.
Records management
Users must not delete, alter, destroy, move or dispose of NDIA records unless this is authorised under approved records management processes.
https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A02796/latest
04 Archives Act 1983
ARC-02
Capture official business information in approved NDIA systems so it can be managed as a record.
Archives Act objects and Commonwealth records obligations; National Archives disposal and records management framework.
Acceptable use should require users to keep business records in repositories that support retention, search and lawful disposal.
Applies to NDIA users who create decisions, advice, approvals, case notes, meeting records, emails, messages or other business evidence.
Approved repositories
Users must store official NDIA business information in approved NDIA systems and must not keep the only copy in personal email, local drives or unapproved services.
https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A02796/latest
04 Archives Act 1983
ARC-03
Preserve records that may be required for FOI, legal, audit, investigation, complaint or parliamentary processes.
Archives Act and records preservation obligations; interaction with FOI and accountability laws.
The AUP must require litigation holds and preservation of potentially relevant records.
Applies across NDIA operations because ICT records may evidence decisions, participant interactions, expenditure and staff conduct.
Legal holds and investigations
Users must preserve NDIA records when asked by Legal, FOI, Privacy, People, Audit, Fraud, Security or Records teams and must not delete or alter relevant information.
https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A02796/latest
05 AG Agencies Privacy Code
AGAPC-01
Implement privacy by design through practices, procedures and systems that support APP compliance.
Privacy (Australian Government Agencies - Governance) APP Code 2017, governance requirements; APP 1.2.
The AUP should require privacy-safe behaviour whenever users access, create, store or share personal information.
NDIA is an Australian Government agency subject to the Privacy Act and handles extensive personal and sensitive information about participants, nominees, providers and staff.
Privacy governance
Users must handle personal information only through approved NDIA systems and processes that are designed to protect privacy.

https://www.oaic.gov.au/privacy/privacy-guidance-for-organisations-and-government-agencies/government-agencies/australian-government-agencies-privacy-code/privacy-australian-government-agencies-governance-app-code-2017
05 AG Agencies Privacy Code
AGAPC-02
Conduct a privacy impact assessment for high privacy risk activities and material changes involving personal information.
Australian Government Agencies Privacy Code PIA requirements.
The AUP should require approval before adopting new tools, integrations or data uses that may affect privacy.
Applies to NDIA users proposing new ICT systems, online forms, analytics, automation, pilots, cloud services or data sharing activities involving personal information.
New systems and tools
Users must not introduce or use new ICT tools, online services, integrations or data uses involving personal information until required privacy and security assessments are completed.
https://www.oaic.gov.au/privacy/privacy-guidance-for-organisations-and-government-agencies/government-agencies/australian-government-agencies-privacy-code
05 AG Agencies Privacy Code
AGAPC-03
Ensure privacy training, awareness and incident reporting are embedded in agency practice.
Australian Government Agencies Privacy Code training and governance requirements.
The AUP should make completion of mandatory privacy training and prompt reporting of issues a condition of ICT access.
Applies to NDIA staff, contractors and partner users who access participant, provider, staff or other personal information.
Training and reporting
Users must complete required privacy training and report suspected privacy incidents, misdirected emails, unauthorised access or data loss immediately through approved NDIA channels.
https://www.oaic.gov.au/privacy/privacy-guidance-for-organisations-and-government-agencies/government-agencies/australian-government-agencies-privacy-code
05 AG Agencies Privacy Code
AGAPC-04
Maintain clear roles and accountabilities for privacy management.
Australian Government Agencies Privacy Code privacy officer, privacy champion and governance requirements.
AUP compliance requires users to know when to escalate privacy questions and not make ad hoc decisions about personal information handling.
Applies to all NDIA users; specialist advice should be sought from privacy, legal or information governance teams.
Escalation and advice
Users must seek privacy advice before handling personal information in a new, unusual or higher risk way.
https://www.oaic.gov.au/privacy/privacy-guidance-for-organisations-and-government-agencies/government-agencies/australian-government-agencies-privacy-code
06 AHRC Act 1986
AHRC-01
Support equal opportunity and prevent unlawful discrimination in conduct that may become the subject of a complaint.
AHRC Act functions relating to human rights, equal opportunity in employment and unlawful discrimination.
The AUP should prohibit discriminatory ICT conduct and preserve evidence for complaint handling.
NDIA is an APS employer and service delivery agency; digital interactions with staff, participants and the public may be reviewed in complaints or investigations.
Respectful and inclusive conduct
Users must use NDIA ICT in a way that respects human rights, equal opportunity and the dignity of all people.
https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A03366/latest
06 AHRC Act 1986
AHRC-02
Cooperate with human rights, discrimination, privacy, integrity or workplace investigations and preserve relevant ICT records.
AHRC Act inquiry, complaint and conciliation functions.
The AUP should direct users not to delete, conceal or alter digital material that may be relevant to complaints.
Applies when NDIA handles workplace complaints, participant complaints, discrimination allegations or other matters involving ICT records.
Investigations and evidence preservation
Users must preserve and provide NDIA ICT records when lawfully required for complaints, reviews, audits or investigations.
https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A03366/latest
06 AHRC Act 1986
AHRC-03
Use accessible and respectful language in digital communications with people with disability and other protected groups.
AHRC Act objects and complaint framework, read with Commonwealth anti-discrimination laws.
Clear, respectful digital communication reduces the risk of conduct inconsistent with human rights obligations.
Applies to all NDIA digital channels, including email, case notes, online meetings, SMS, letters, portals and public content.
Accessible communications
Users must communicate through NDIA ICT in a respectful, inclusive and accessible manner.
https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A03366/latest
07 Australian Privacy Principle
APP-01
Manage personal information openly and transparently and follow approved privacy practices.
APP 1 - open and transparent management of personal information.
The AUP must direct users to follow NDIA privacy policies and approved handling practices.
NDIA is an APP entity and holds large volumes of personal and sensitive information.
Privacy obligations
Users must handle personal information in accordance with NDIA privacy policies, notices and approved business processes.
https://www.oaic.gov.au/privacy/australian-privacy-principles
07 Australian Privacy Principle
APP-02
Collect personal information only where reasonably necessary for NDIA functions and by lawful and fair means.
APP 3 and APP 4 - collection of solicited and unsolicited personal information.
AUP rules should prevent unnecessary collection in emails, spreadsheets, notes, screenshots, recordings and collaboration tools.
Applies to participant, nominee, provider, staff, complaint, health, disability and identity information handled through NDIA ICT.
Collection minimisation
Users must only collect personal information that is necessary for authorised NDIA work and must not ask for or record unnecessary personal information.
https://www.oaic.gov.au/privacy/australian-privacy-principles/australian-privacy-principles-guidelines
07 Australian Privacy Principle
APP-03
Use or disclose personal information only for authorised purposes or where an APP exception applies.
APP 6 - use or disclosure of personal information.
The AUP must prohibit casual, curiosity-based, convenience-based or unauthorised sharing of personal information.
Applies to all NDIA records, messages, attachments, case notes, reports and system outputs containing personal information.
Use and disclosure
Users must not use, discuss, copy, send, upload or disclose personal information unless it is required for authorised NDIA work and permitted by law and policy.
https://www.oaic.gov.au/privacy/australian-privacy-principles
07 Australian Privacy Principle
APP-04
Do not disclose personal information overseas or to unapproved external cloud services without authorisation.
APP 8 - cross-border disclosure of personal information.
AUP controls should stop users from placing personal information into unapproved online services or overseas-hosted tools.
Applies to external file sharing, cloud storage, online translation, generative AI, analytics, email forwarding and supplier tools.
External services and cloud use
Users must not upload, enter, sync or send NDIA personal information to external or overseas services unless the service and disclosure are approved.
https://www.oaic.gov.au/privacy/australian-privacy-principles
07 Australian Privacy Principle
APP-05
Take reasonable steps to protect personal information from misuse, interference, loss and unauthorised access, modification or disclosure.
APP 11 - security of personal information.
The AUP must set security behaviours for passwords, devices, sharing, storage, printing, remote work and reporting incidents.
Applies to all users accessing NDIA personal information from any location or device.
Security of personal information
Users must protect personal information from loss, misuse and unauthorised access by using approved systems, secure devices, strong authentication and approved sharing methods.
https://www.oaic.gov.au/privacy/australian-privacy-principles
07 Australian Privacy Principle
APP-06
Support access and correction rights by keeping personal information accurate, complete and retrievable.
APP 10, APP 12 and APP 13 - quality, access and correction.
The AUP should require accurate entries and preservation of records so NDIA can respond to access and correction requests.
Applies to case notes, participant records, provider records, emails, attachments and system data.
Data quality and correction
Users must take reasonable care to ensure personal information they enter or update in NDIA systems is accurate, relevant and complete.
https://www.oaic.gov.au/privacy/australian-privacy-principles
08 Copyright Act 1968 Cth
COPY-01
Do not reproduce, communicate, download, upload, stream or share copyrighted material without permission, licence or statutory authority.
Copyright Act 1968 exclusive rights and infringement provisions, including ss 31, 36 and 101.
The AUP must prevent unlawful use of copyright material through NDIA devices, networks, email, collaboration platforms and websites.
Applies to all users who create, copy, store, publish, email, present or share material using NDIA ICT.
Copyright and intellectual property
Users must not use NDIA ICT to copy, store, share, publish or stream copyright material unless they have an NDIA-approved right to do so.
https://www.legislation.gov.au/C1968A00063/latest
08 Copyright Act 1968 Cth
COPY-02
Use software, fonts, images, audio, video, datasets and publications only under approved licences and terms.
Copyright Act rights in works and subject matter other than works; licensing obligations.
ICT acceptable use must address software and content licensing because infringement can arise from unlicensed copying or distribution.
Applies to staff and contractors installing software, using stock images, creating presentations, using datasets or developing public content.
Software and content licensing
Users must only install or use software and digital content that has been approved, licensed or otherwise authorised for NDIA use.
https://www.legislation.gov.au/C1968A00063/latest
08 Copyright Act 1968 Cth
COPY-03
Do not bypass technological protection measures or remove rights management information.
Copyright Act Part V, Division 2A - technological protection measures and electronic rights management information.
The AUP must prohibit circumvention and tampering with protections on digital content or software.
Applies to NDIA devices, browser extensions, media tools, software packages and content downloaded or shared for work.
Prohibited activities
Users must not use NDIA ICT to bypass digital locks, licence controls or rights management information on software or content.
https://www.legislation.gov.au/C1968A00063/latest
09 Criminal Code Act 1995
CCA-01
Prohibit unauthorised access, modification or impairment of data, systems and electronic communications.
Criminal Code, Part 10.7 computer offences, including Divisions 477 and 478.
The AUP must make clear that unauthorised system access, hacking, malware, data tampering and impairment are prohibited.
Applies to NDIA systems, participant records, supplier systems, external services and any device or network used for NDIA work.
Security and prohibited conduct
Users must not attempt to bypass security, access systems or information without authorisation, alter data improperly, introduce malware or impair any ICT service.
https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A04868/latest
09 Criminal Code Act 1995
CCA-02
Prohibit use of carriage services for menacing, harassing, offensive, abusive or unlawful communications.
Criminal Code, Part 10.6 telecommunications offences, including carriage service offences.
ICT acceptable use must address unlawful digital communications via email, messaging, phones, online meetings, social platforms and SMS.
Applies to all NDIA communications channels and devices, including official and work-related online accounts.
Digital communications
Users must not use NDIA ICT to threaten, harass, abuse, menace, stalk, exploit, groom or unlawfully offend any person.
https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A04868/latest
09 Criminal Code Act 1995
CCA-03
Prohibit creation, possession, transmission or access to unlawful material using NDIA ICT.
Criminal Code offences relating to child abuse material, abhorrent violent material, intimate images and other unlawful content.
The AUP must protect NDIA systems from illegal material and require immediate reporting.
Applies to all NDIA users, devices, networks, storage locations, collaboration tools and remote access connections.
Illegal material
Users must not use NDIA ICT to access, store, create, transmit or distribute illegal material and must report accidental exposure immediately.
https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A04868/latest
09 Criminal Code Act 1995
CCA-04
Prohibit doxxing and misuse of personal data to menace, harass or cause harm where criminal offences apply.
Criminal Code provisions as amended by Privacy and Other Legislation Amendment Act 2024, Schedule 3.
The AUP should expressly prohibit publication or sharing of personal data for harassment or harm.
Applies to personal information about participants, staff, providers, complainants, witnesses and members of the public.
Personal information misuse
Users must not use NDIA ICT to publish, share or threaten to share personal information for harassment, intimidation, retaliation or harm.
https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A04868/latest
10 Disability Discrimination Ac
DDA-01
Do not discriminate against people because of disability in work, services or administration of Commonwealth programs.
Disability Discrimination Act 1992, ss 5-6, 15, 24 and 29.
The AUP must prevent discriminatory digital conduct and barriers in NDIA ICT-enabled services.
Central to NDIA operations because the agency serves people with disability and employs people with disability.
Inclusion and non-discrimination
Users must not use NDIA ICT to exclude, disadvantage, mock, stereotype or treat a person unfavourably because of disability.
https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A04426/latest
10 Disability Discrimination Ac
DDA-02
Provide accessible digital information and reasonable adjustments where needed.
DDA provisions on goods, services, facilities and Commonwealth programs; reasonable adjustment principles.
The AUP should require accessible digital content and approved alternative formats when needed.
Applies to websites, portals, forms, documents, emails, templates, videos, online meetings and participant communications.
Accessibility
Users must create and share NDIA digital information in accessible formats and provide reasonable adjustments through approved processes when required.
https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A04426/latest
10 Disability Discrimination Ac
DDA-03
Prevent disability-based harassment or hostile digital environments.
DDA harassment and discrimination provisions.
Acceptable use must prohibit disability harassment in email, chat, case notes, online meetings and social platforms.
Applies to staff interactions and communications with participants, nominees, carers, providers and the public.
Respectful ICT use
Users must not use NDIA ICT to harass, ridicule, shame or demean a person because of disability, impairment, support needs or assistive technology use.
https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A04426/latest
10 Disability Discrimination Ac
DDA-04
Do not create or publish digital content that cannot be used with common assistive technologies unless an approved accessible alternative is provided.
DDA service and facilities obligations, read with Australian Government digital accessibility expectations.
NDIA digital services must be usable by people with disability; the AUP should make accessibility a user responsibility.
Applies to staff and contractors who publish documents, forms, images, dashboards, intranet pages, videos or public content.
Digital publishing
Users must not publish NDIA digital content unless accessibility has been considered and known accessibility issues have been fixed or an approved alternative is available.
https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A04426/latest
11 Essential Eight Maturity Mod
Apply application control by limiting execution to approved applications and scripts.
Essential Eight Maturity Model - application control.
The AUP must prohibit unapproved software, scripts and executables because user behaviour can bypass application control.
Applies to NDIA-managed devices, virtual desktops, cloud workspaces and any endpoint used for NDIA work.
Software and application use
Users must not install, run or attempt to run unapproved software, scripts, extensions or executables on NDIA ICT.
https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/essential-eight/essential-eight-maturity-model
11 Essential Eight Maturity Mod
Support patching of applications and operating systems.
Essential Eight Maturity Model - patch applications and patch operating systems.
Users must not block or defer required updates because patching is a core cyber control.
Applies to NDIA-managed devices and approved BYOD or partner devices where used for NDIA access.
Device maintenance
Users must keep NDIA ICT connected, updated and available for security patching and must not disable update, security or management controls.
https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/essential-eight/essential-eight-maturity-model
11 Essential Eight Maturity Mod
Restrict administrative privileges and enforce strong authentication.
Essential Eight Maturity Model - restrict administrative privileges and multi-factor authentication.
The AUP must prohibit credential sharing and unauthorised privileged use.
Applies to all NDIA accounts, privileged accounts, service accounts and administrator access.
Accounts and authentication
Users must use their own NDIA account, protect credentials and MFA factors, and must not share passwords, tokens or privileged access.
https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/essential-eight/essential-eight-maturity-model
11 Essential Eight Maturity Mod
Control Microsoft Office macros and harden user applications.
Essential Eight Maturity Model - configure Microsoft Office macro settings and user application hardening.
Many compromises begin with malicious documents and browser/email behaviours; the AUP should make safe use explicit.
Applies to documents, email attachments, browsers, PDF tools, collaboration platforms and productivity applications.
Email, web and documents
Users must not enable macros, active content, browser plug-ins or risky document features unless approved for a genuine work purpose.
https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/essential-eight/essential-eight-maturity-model
11 Essential Eight Maturity Mod
Maintain reliable backups by storing official information in approved repositories.
Essential Eight Maturity Model - regular backups.
AUP rules should stop data being stored only on local drives or unapproved services where backups and recovery are weak.
Applies to NDIA files, emails, case material, datasets, reports, configuration records and system documentation.
Storage and backup
Users must store official NDIA information in approved repositories so it is backed up, recoverable and managed as a record.
https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/essential-eight/essential-eight-maturity-model
12 Fair Work Act 2009 Cth
FWA-01
Prevent bullying, harassment, sexual harassment, intimidation and other unlawful workplace conduct using ICT.
Fair Work Act workplace protections, anti-bullying and sexual harassment provisions.
The AUP must set clear standards for electronic conduct in the workplace.
Applies to NDIA workers and work-related ICT communications, including remote and hybrid work.
Respectful ICT use
Users must not use NDIA ICT to bully, sexually harass, intimidate, victimise, shame or repeatedly behave unreasonably towards another worker.
https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2009A00028/latest
12 Fair Work Act 2009 Cth
FWA-02
Protect workplace rights and prevent adverse action or coercion through digital channels.
Fair Work Act general protections and workplace rights provisions.
The AUP should prohibit misuse of ICT to pressure, threaten, retaliate against or disadvantage workers exercising workplace rights.
Applies to communications about leave, complaints, flexible work, union activity, workplace rights, performance processes and whistleblowing.
Workplace rights
Users must not use NDIA ICT to threaten, coerce, retaliate against or disadvantage a person because they exercise a workplace right or raise a workplace concern.
https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2009A00028/latest
12 Fair Work Act 2009 Cth
FWA-03
Respect the right to disconnect and manage out-of-hours contact reasonably.
Fair Work Act right to disconnect provisions.
An ICT AUP should set expectations for after-hours messages, alerts and response requirements.
Applies to NDIA employees and managers using email, chat, calls, SMS and collaboration platforms outside working hours.
Out-of-hours communications
Users must not require or pressure employees to monitor, read or respond to work communications outside working hours unless the contact is reasonable and authorised.
https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2009A00028/latest
12 Fair Work Act 2009 Cth
FWA-04
Keep workplace records and communications accurate and professional.
Fair Work Act workplace protections and recordkeeping context.
ICT records can be evidence in employment matters; the AUP should require professionalism and accuracy.
Applies to people records, emails, performance notes, meeting records, rostering, leave and workplace relations systems.
Workplace records
Users must ensure workplace-related entries and communications in NDIA ICT are accurate, respectful, relevant and appropriate for an official record.
https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2009A00028/latest
13 Freedom of Information Act 1
FOI-01
Recognise that electronic documents held by NDIA may be subject to FOI access rights.
FOI Act objects and right of access provisions, including ss 3, 11 and 15.
The AUP should remind users that emails, messages, documents, metadata and system records can be official documents.
Applies to all NDIA ICT records, including documents held by contractors for NDIA purposes where applicable.
Official records and FOI
Users must create and manage NDIA ICT records as official documents that may be accessed under FOI or other legal processes.
https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A02562/latest
13 Freedom of Information Act 1
